correctness.rationale: For any frame, B_0=empty and B_{k+1}={x: exists y accessible from x with every successor of y in B_k} are exactly the increasing failure sets of (box diamond)^k top. The minimal-rank contradiction shows every finite-failure world has an infinite-failure successor. A new failure at rank k induces k distinct strictly descending finite ranks and k pairwise distinct infinite-rank witnesses, proving at least 2k worlds. The path on 2m+2 worlds has first failure rank m+1 at its initial world. The standalone verifier independently enumerated every relation up to four worlds and checked direct semantics, ranks and ladder witnesses, plus seeded random frames and paths up to depth 50; these finite checks are not used as the all-parameter proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Prior: for every m, a separating frame of 2m+2 worlds exists (upper bound); and for m in {1,2,3} no smaller frame works (finite cases). New: for every m>=1 no smaller frame works (universal lower bound). The two previous assertions do not logically imply the universal lower bound. Conversely the new theorem incorporates and generalizes precisely the already known finite instances.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 literature posed first distinguishing frame cardinalities and gave 2m+2 upper bounds with only three exact SAT-certified cases. An all-parameter exact lower bound resolves that natural gap rather than an arbitrary slice, determines the first possible frame size for each depth, and isolates the structural mechanism (finite-rank and permanent-survivor witnesses).
